shlokas.sanskrit: तथोक्तवति रामे तु तस्य जन्म तदद्भुतम् । उवाच लक्ष्मणो भूयो भरतश्च महायशाः ।। 7.90.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathoktavati rāme tu tasya janma tadadbhutam | uvāca lakṣmaṇo bhūyo bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ || 7.90.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When Rama had thus told of his wondrous birth, Lakshmana and the greatly renowned Bharata spoke to him once more.

shlokas.sanskrit: इला सा सोमपुत्रस्य संवत्सरमथोषिता । अकरोत्किं नरश्रेष्ठ तत्त्वं शंसितुमर्हसि ।। 7.90.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ilā sā somaputrasya saṃvatsaramathoṣitā | akarotkiṃ naraśreṣṭha tattvaṃ śaṃsitumarhasi || 7.90.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "O best of men, when that Ila had dwelt for a year as the wife of the son of Soma, what did she do? You are worthy to tell us the truth of it."

shlokas.sanskrit: तयोस्तद्वाक्यमाधुर्यं निशम्य परिपृच्छतोः । रामः पुनरुवाचेमां प्रजापतिसुते कथाम् ।। 7.90.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tayostadvākyamādhuryaṃ niśamya paripṛcchatoḥ | rāmaḥ punaruvācemāṃ prajāpatisute kathām || 7.90.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing the sweetness of the words of those two as they inquired, Rama, O son of the Lord of Creatures, related this tale again.

shlokas.sanskrit: पुरुषत्वं गते शूरे बुधः परमबुद्धिमान् । संवर्तं परमोदारमाजुहाव महायशाः ।। 7.90.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: puruṣatvaṃ gate śūre budhaḥ paramabuddhimān | saṃvartaṃ paramodāramājuhāva mahāyaśāḥ || 7.90.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When the hero had attained manhood, the supremely wise and greatly renowned Budha summoned the most generous Samvarta.

shlokas.sanskrit: च्यवनं भृगुपुत्रं च मुनिं चारिष्टनेमिनम् । प्रमोदनं मोदकरं ततो दुर्वाससं मुनिम् ।। 7.90.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: cyavanaṃ bhṛguputraṃ ca muniṃ cāriṣṭaneminam | pramodanaṃ modakaraṃ tato durvāsasaṃ munim || 7.90.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And Chyavana the son of Bhrigu, and the sage Arishtanemi, and Pramodana the bringer of joy, and then the sage Durvasas.

shlokas.sanskrit: एतान्सर्वान्समानीय वाक्यज्ञस्तत्त्वदर्शनः । उवाच सर्वान्सुहृदो धैर्येण सुसमाहितान् ।। 7.90.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: etānsarvānsamānīya vākyajñastattvadarśanaḥ | uvāca sarvānsuhṛdo dhairyeṇa susamāhitān || 7.90.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having gathered all these together, that knower of speech and perceiver of truth addressed all his friends, who were resolute and well composed in spirit.

shlokas.sanskrit: अयं राजा महाबाहुः कर्दमस्य इलः सुतः । जानीतैनं यथाभूतं श्रेयो ह्यत्र विधीयताम् ।। 7.90.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ayaṃ rājā mahābāhuḥ kardamasya ilaḥ sutaḥ | jānītainaṃ yathābhūtaṃ śreyo hyatra vidhīyatām || 7.90.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This mighty-armed king is Ila, the son of Kardama. Know him as he truly is, and let his welfare be devised in this matter."

shlokas.sanskrit: तेषां संवदतामेव तमाश्रममुपागमत् । कर्दमस्तु महातेजा द्विजैः सह महात्मभिः ।। 7.90.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāmeva tamāśramamupāgamat | kardamastu mahātejā dvijaiḥ saha mahātmabhiḥ || 7.90.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Even as they were conversing, the greatly resplendent Kardama, together with high-souled Brahmins, came to that hermitage.

shlokas.sanskrit: पुलस्त्यश्च क्रतुश्चैव वषट्कारस्तथैव च । ओङ्कारश्च महातेजास्तमाश्रममुपागमत् ।। 7.90.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pulastyaśca kratuścaiva vaṣaṭkārastathaiva ca | oṅkāraśca mahātejāstamāśramamupāgamat || 7.90.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And Pulastya, and Kratu, and likewise Vashatkara, and the greatly resplendent Omkara came to that hermitage.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसः परस्परसमागमे । हितैषिणो बाल्हिपतेः पृथग्वाक्यान्यथाब्रुवन् ।। 7.90.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te sarve hṛṣṭamanasaḥ parasparasamāgame | hitaiṣiṇo bālhipateḥ pṛthagvākyānyathābruvan || 7.90.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: All of them, glad of heart at meeting one another, wishing well to the lord of Balhi, each spoke their words in turn.

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्दमस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं सुतार्थं परमं हितम् । द्विजाः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यच्छ्रेयः पार्थिवस्य हि ।। 7.90.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kardamastvabravīdvākyaṃ sutārthaṃ paramaṃ hitam | dvijāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ yacchreyaḥ pārthivasya hi || 7.90.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Kardama spoke a word for his son's sake, supremely beneficial: "O Brahmins, hear my word, which is for the welfare of the king."

shlokas.sanskrit: नान्यं पश्यामि भैषज्यमन्तरा वृषभध्वजम् । नाश्वमेधात्परो यज्ञः प्रियश्चैव महात्मनः । तस्माद्यजामहे सर्वे पार्थिवार्थे दुरासदम् ।। 7.90.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nānyaṃ paśyāmi bhaiṣajyamantarā vṛṣabhadhvajam | nāśvamedhātparo yajñaḥ priyaścaiva mahātmanaḥ | tasmādyajāmahe sarve pārthivārthe durāsadam || 7.90.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I see no other remedy save the god whose banner bears the bull. There is no sacrifice higher than the horse-sacrifice, and it is dear to the great-souled one. Therefore let us all perform, for the king's sake, that rite hard for others to accomplish."

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्दमेनैवमुक्तास्तु सर्व एव द्विजर्षभाः । रोचयन्ति स्म तं यज्ञं रुद्रस्याराधनं प्रति ।। 7.90.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kardamenaivamuktāstu sarva eva dvijarṣabhāḥ | rocayanti sma taṃ yajñaṃ rudrasyārādhanaṃ prati || 7.90.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus addressed by Kardama, all those bulls among the twice-born approved of that sacrifice as a means of propitiating Rudra.

shlokas.sanskrit: संवर्तस्य तु राजर्षेः शिष्यः पुरपुरञ्जयः । मरुत्त इति विख्यातस्तं यज्ञं समुपाहरत् ।। 7.90.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: saṃvartasya tu rājarṣeḥ śiṣyaḥ purapurañjayaḥ | marutta iti vikhyātastaṃ yajñaṃ samupāharat || 7.90.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the disciple of the royal sage Samvarta, the conqueror of enemy cities, renowned by the name Marutta, undertook that sacrifice.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो यज्ञो महानासीद्बुधाश्रमसमीपतः । रुद्रश्च परमं तोषमाजगाम महायशाः ।। 7.90.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato yajño mahānāsīdbudhāśramasamīpataḥ | rudraśca paramaṃ toṣamājagāma mahāyaśāḥ || 7.90.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then a great sacrifice took place near the hermitage of Budha, and the illustrious Rudra came thither, attaining the highest satisfaction.

shlokas.sanskrit: अथ यज्ञे समाप्ते तु प्रीतः परमया मुदा । उमापतिर्द्विजान्सर्वानुवाच इलसन्निधौ ।। 7.90.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: atha yajñe samāpte tu prītaḥ paramayā mudā | umāpatirdvijānsarvānuvāca ilasannidhau || 7.90.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Now, when the sacrifice was completed, the Lord of Uma, pleased and filled with the utmost joy, spoke to all the twice-born in the presence of Ila.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रीतो ऽस्मि हयमेधेन भक्त्या च द्विजसत्तमाः । अस्य बाह्लिपतेश्चैव किं करोमि प्रियं शुभम् ।। 7.90.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: prīto 'smi hayamedhena bhaktyā ca dvijasattamāḥ | asya bāhlipateścaiva kiṃ karomi priyaṃ śubham || 7.90.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I am pleased by this horse-sacrifice and by your devotion, O best of the twice-born. What pleasant and auspicious thing may I do for this lord of Bahli?"

shlokas.sanskrit: तथा वदति देवेशे द्विजास्ते सुसमाहिताः । प्रसादयन्ति देवेशं यथा स्यात्पुरुषस्त्विला ।। 7.90.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathā vadati deveśe dvijāste susamāhitāḥ | prasādayanti deveśaṃ yathā syātpuruṣastvilā || 7.90.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When the Lord of the gods spoke thus, those twice-born ones, well-composed, propitiated the Lord of the gods so that Ila might become a man.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः प्रीतो महादेवः पुरुषत्वं ददौ पुनः । इलायै सुमहातेजा दत्त्वा चान्तरधीयत ।। 7.90.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ puruṣatvaṃ dadau punaḥ | ilāyai sumahātejā dattvā cāntaradhīyata || 7.90.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the great god, pleased, the one of mighty splendor, granted manhood once more to Ila, and having granted it, vanished.

shlokas.sanskrit: निवृत्ते हयमेधे च गतश्चादर्शनं हरः । यथागतं द्विजाः सर्वे ह्यगच्छन्दीर्घदर्शिनः ।। 7.90.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nivṛtte hayamedhe ca gataścādarśanaṃ haraḥ | yathāgataṃ dvijāḥ sarve hyagacchandīrghadarśinaḥ || 7.90.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And when the horse-sacrifice had ended, Hara departed from sight, and all those far-seeing twice-born ones went back as they had come.

shlokas.sanskrit: राजा तु बाह्लिमुत्सृज्य मध्यदेशे ह्यनुत्तमम् । निवेशयामास पुरं प्रतिष्ठानं यशस्करम् ।। 7.90.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rājā tu bāhlimutsṛjya madhyadeśe hyanuttamam | niveśayāmāsa puraṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ yaśaskaram || 7.90.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the king, leaving Bahli behind, founded in the central region a most excellent and glory-bringing city called Pratishthana.

shlokas.sanskrit: शशबिन्दुश्च राजर्षिर्बाह्लिं पुरपुरञ्जयः । प्रतिष्ठाने इलो राजा प्रजापतिसुतो बली ।। 7.90.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śaśabinduśca rājarṣirbāhliṃ purapurañjayaḥ | pratiṣṭhāne ilo rājā prajāpatisuto balī || 7.90.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the royal sage Shashabindu, vanquisher of the cities of his foes, ruled Bahli, while in Pratishthana ruled King Ila, the mighty son of the Prajapati.

shlokas.sanskrit: स काले प्राप्तवाँल्लोकमिलो ब्राह्ममनुत्तमम् । ऐलः पुरूरवा राजा प्रतिष्ठानमवाप्तवान् ।। 7.90.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa kāle prāptavāँllokamilo brāhmamanuttamam | ailaḥ purūravā rājā pratiṣṭhānamavāptavān || 7.90.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: In time that Ila attained the supreme world of Brahma; and his son, King Pururavas the Aila, obtained Pratishthana.

shlokas.sanskrit: ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रभावः पुरुषर्षभौ । स्त्रीभूतः पौरुषं लेभे यच्चान्यदपि दुर्लभम् ।। 7.90.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: īdṛśo hyaśvamedhasya prabhāvaḥ puruṣarṣabhau | strībhūtaḥ pauruṣaṃ lebhe yaccānyadapi durlabham || 7.90.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Such, O you two bulls among men, is the power of the horse-sacrifice, by which one who had become a woman regained his manhood, and gained also other things hard to obtain.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवतितमः सर्गः ।। 90 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe navatitamaḥ sargaḥ || 90 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the ninetieth canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana, the first poem composed by the sage Valmiki.
